newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN 1997 GRAIN CROP SEEN SLIGHTLY HIGHER-AGMIN.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN 1997 GRAIN CROP SEEN SLIGHTLY HIGHER-AGMIN.

text.p: Germany's 1997 grain crop may slightly exceed last year's 42.1 million, the Bonn farm ministry said in a press release on Friday, citing information obtained from the national statistics office.
Yields should be satisfactory but below those last year, assuming normal weather from now up to the end of harvesting, it said.
But the volume should still be higher because of area expansions resulting from a cut in land set-aside rates.
Harvesting of barley in the second half of July was often disrupted by rainfall, the ministry said.
Weather patterns in August have been drier and sunnier.
Grain trader Toepfer on Thursday maintained a forecast for a 43 million tonnes crop in 1997, citing area expansions and good barley qualities despite the unfavourable harvest weather.
